We have template 1914398. The retro_smarts_template shows a transformation: It seems to be a substitution of a bromine on an aromatic ring with something else? Let's parse.

retro_smarts_template: '[#7;+:2]-[c:3]1:[c:4]:[c:5]:[c:6](-[#8:7]-[C:8](-[C:9])(-[C:10])-[C:11]):[c;H0;D3;+0:12](-[Br;H0;D1;+0:1]):[c:13]:1>>Br-[Br;H0;D1;+0:1].[#7;+:2]-[c:3]1:[c:4]:[c:5]:[c:6](-[#8:7]-[C:8](-[C:9])(-[C:10])-[C:11]):[cH;D2;+0:12]:[c:13]:1'

So forward reaction (retro direction) is product (left side) to precursors (right side). The left side is a molecule with a bromine attached to aromatic carbon (c;H0;D3;+0:12) and also a nitrogen attached to aromatic (maybe anilide). The right side gives Br-Br (bromine dimer?) and the same aromatic but with a hydrogen at that position (cH). So the template is a bromination? Actually retro: product has Br attached, precursors are Br-Br (bromine) and the same aromatic without Br (hydrogen). So applying retro template to a target molecule that contains a bromine on aromatic will give two precursors: bromine (as Br) and the de-brominated aromatic.

Our target molecule: "CC(=O)OC1=CC=CC=C1C(=O)O". That's phenyl acetate? Actually it's phenyl acetate with carboxylic acid? Let's decode: CC(=O)O is acetate group attached to aromatic carbon? The SMILES: CC(=O)O C1=CC=CC=C1 C(=O)O. So it's phenyl acetate (acetoxy) and carboxylic acid para? Actually it's 4-acetoxybenzoic acid (p-acetoxybenzoic acid). No bromine present. So template likely not applicable because no Br. That's why apply_template returned empty.

Thus there are no precursors using this template. The answer should be empty list [].
